source.title: The loss surface and expressivity of deep convolutional neural networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a numerical training experiment and theoretical analysis of whether wide CNNs can attain zero training error, using MNIST and squared loss rather than the benchmark recipes emphasized in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The numerical experiment reports training loss and error across filter widths. Theorems provide existence and loss-surface results under stated assumptions, but are not additional empirical training outcomes. References to Zhang et al. (2017) are cited prior work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures CNN training classification error after Adam training in a new setting: MNIST with sigmoid activations and squared loss. This bears on V1's near-zero training-error behavior, although it does not establish the specified CIFAR results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that their expressivity and conditional loss-landscape results help explain effective CNN training. Their theorem establishes zero loss at every critical point in the specified full-rank set when the wide layer is followed by a fully connected layer; it does not guarantee optimizer convergence or exclude bad minima outside that set. Cross-entropy is outside their analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The numerical study uses MNIST, sigmoid CNNs, squared loss, Adam with decaying learning rate, and 2000 epochs; the theoretical analysis gives existence and critical-point conditions rather than testing the listed benchmark training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: First-layer filter count changes the reported training error: T1 = 10 and 20 have nonzero error; T1 ≥ 30 has zero error.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems establish finite-sample expressivity and zero-loss critical points within a specified full-rank parameter set under architectural and activation assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable wide CNNs can represent arbitrary finite training targets, and when the wide layer is followed by a fully connected layer, every critical point in the specified full-rank set has zero squared loss. These results do not establish gradient-training convergence or V2's teacher-student minimum frequencies.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), as stated in the supplied paper text
record.problems: The experiment is limited to one MNIST CNN setup and filter-count sweep, with no stated controls or uncertainty estimates. Theoretical guarantees apply only under the paper's architectural, activation, rank and loss assumptions; the authors note their analysis does not fit cross-entropy loss.
record.rows_left_out: None; all ten separately reported filter-count training-error values in Table 2 were extracted.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; SGD; early stopping and regularization comparisons; substantial training error in smaller models. The experimental initialization is not specified.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student training, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Initialization comparisons measuring training speed or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons and normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed limits_scope verdict for R1–R2: their residual errors are already near zero. Input perturbations are not label corruption. The supplied paper identifies its venue as ICML 2018, not ICLR.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a CNN on MNIST with sigmoid activations, Adam, decaying learning rate and squared loss. Does not test CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, SGD, or the stated small-model, early-stopping and regularization comparisons.
No teacher-student two-layer ReLU experiments or neuron-count comparison.
No depth sweep comparing plain and residual networks.
No comparison of initialization schemes or initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability or curvature experiment.
